quotes.quote: Watching, Reasoning, and Searching: A Video Deep Research Benchmark on Open Web for Agentic Video Reasoning
Watching, Reasoning and Searching: A Video Deep Research Benchmark
we construct the first video deep research benchmark, VideoDR
Agentic is not consistently superior to Workflow: its gains depend on a model
its gains depend on a model's ability to maintain the initial video anchors over long retrieval chains
goal drift and long-horizon consistency are the core bottlenecks
we propose VideoDR, the first open-domain benchmark that systematically evaluates video deep research
We propose Video Deep Research (VideoDR): an open-domain factoid question answering benchmark conditioned on a given video
the model is not allowed to repeatedly re-watch the video
Formally, the VideoDR task can be expressed as: f : (V, Q; S) → A.
we recruited three annotators with experience in video understanding and web search
single-scene clips with highly redundant visual semantics
multi-frame reasoning: each question must be grounded in video cues spanning multiple frames
multi-hop reasoning: each question must implicitly admit a decomposable multi-step reasoning path
we archived the web pages containing the key evidence supporting each answer
Only samples that fail under both of the following conditions are retained as valid
the annotator is only given the textual question q and can conduct the web search
the annotator answers the question by watching only the video v
five independent participants solving the tasks in a blind manner
Across all 500 samples, the mean sample-level success rate is s̄ = 0.4022 with a standard deviation of 0.298
Finally, we construct 500 VideoDR samples.
Daily Life accounting for 33.6%, Technology 22.6%, Culture 13.0%, History 11.8%, Economics 11.4%, and Geography 7.6%.
The average question length is 25.54 tokens
32.4% Short, 30.2% Medium, and 37.4% Long.
we adopt an LLM-as-judge protocol (Zheng et al., 2023) using DeepSeek-V3-0324
The judge outputs a binary correctness label, which we use to compute overall Accuracy.
Gemini-3.1-pro-preview leads under both paradigms, achieving 51.80% under Workflow and 53.60% under Agentic.
GPT-5.4 demonstrates the second-best overall performance, with 47.00% under Workflow and 47.40% under Agentic.
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B achieving 35.00% / 34.60% and Gemma-4-31B-it achieving 31.60% / 33.60%
InternVL3.5-14B reaching 16.00% / 15.40% and GLM-4.6V-Flash reaching 17.80% / 21.80%
only Gemini-3.1-pro-preview and GPT-5.4 consistently surpass the human average under this evaluation setting.
Human performance decreases from 81.71% to 49.64% and then to 11.39%
we conclude that under current mainstream model capabilities, Agentic is not necessarily superior to Workflow
in Agentic, the model cannot re-watch the video during research
Workflow externalizes video cues into an intermediate textual representation, effectively providing a repeatedly accessible external memory
As shown in Table 3, Gemini-3.1-pro-preview benefits from Agentic in History, Technology, and Daily Life, improving from 52.54%→59.32%, 50.44%→54.87%, and 57.74%→60.12%, respectively.
it improves in Geography and Technology (44.74%→55.26%, 39.82%→46.02%)
We further break down the errors into eight categories
Gemini-3.1-pro-preview has the lowest overall error count among all models, with 241 total errors under Workflow and 232 under Agentic
numerical reliability constitutes a distinct and persistent weakness for current MLLMs
It requires models to extract multi-frame visual anchors, turn them into searchable queries, retrieve open-web evidence, and perform multi-hop reasoning to produce verifiable factual answers.
the number of search calls and reasoning steps is not monotonically correlated with accuracy
What determines performance is not using search more, but whether a model can turn a limited number of search calls into a high-quality evidence chain.
Constructing VideoDR requires substantial manual effort because each sample must satisfy both video dependency and web dependency
although this process is time-consuming and limits rapid scaling
